articles.title_ru: ‘It struck me as a minimalist tableau’: Henk Stam’s best phone picture
articles.preview_en: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says.
articles.preview_ru: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says.
articles.full_en: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says. Sixty years ago, he received his first camera for his 11th birthday. The advent of a newer technology initially stumped him. “My first portable phone, that we used to call ‘a brick’, had a terrible camera that took fuzzy pictures. But like everyone, I noticed the steady improvements,” he says. This photo was taken in Portlantis, a visitors’ centre in the Port of Rotterdam that opened in spring 2025. Stam spent his working life in Canada but was born in the Netherlands and returned there on retirement.
